office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering taxes, school funding, housing rules, health policy and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Open seat left by retiring Republican Rep. Carolyn Eslick. Democrat Ida Keeley, a former juvenile court and child-welfare administrator, faces Republican Steve Ewing, a former Lake Stevens councilmember running on low taxes, balanced budgets and public safety.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate and former juvenile court and DCYF administrator running on affordability, school and special-education funding, and public safety that combines accountability with prevention.
highlights: More than 25 years in court, child-welfare and juvenile-justice administration; founding member of Dawson Place [S1][S3]
Supports staffed, trained law enforcement alongside behavioral-health, treatment and youth-intervention investments [S2]
Supports a pause on new high-capacity data centers and enforceable AI standards [S2]
Pledges to fully fund public schools and special education [S1][S2]

safety.basis: Explicitly pairs law-enforcement staffing and accountability with prevention, treatment and youth-intervention spending.

spending.basis: Wants to expand affordable housing and childcare, protect economic-security programs and fully fund schools, while also stressing stewardship of tax dollars.

tech.basis: Supports a pause on new high-capacity data centers until safeguards exist and enforceable AI standards.

experience.basis: First-time candidate, though with a long public-administration career; opponent has six years of city council service.

candidates.summary: Former Lake Stevens councilmember (2019-2025) and Department of Corrections hearings officer running on low taxes, balanced budgets, public safety and 'normal' government.
highlights: Says he passed balanced budgets and opposed higher taxes on the city council [S1]
Calls for 'taxes that are spent wisely and kept low' [S2]
Calls statewide limits on police 'extremism'; endorsed by WACOPS [S1][S2]
Endorsed by the 39th District's Republican delegation [S1]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet and site both pledge low taxes and say he opposed higher taxes; claims are his own, with no independently reviewed votes.

spending.basis: Emphasizes balanced budgets and taxes 'spent wisely'; no specific cuts proposed.

safety.basis: Calls statewide limits on police an 'extremism' to reverse and is endorsed by WACOPS.

experience.basis: Six years on the Lake Stevens City Council plus planning, health and library boards; never served in the Legislature.
